nodes.label: THE FULL REGISTER — every entry ever written
nodes.rationale: A flat append-only record of entries 165-1700: every fault, correction, measurement and ruling is written down rather than repaired silently, so that a wrong claim and its withdrawal both remain readable.

nodes.label: Λ (the index of 976 cells)
nodes.rationale: Defined as the 976 words in {0,1}^17 that are down-sets of A.19's generators; joins are bitwise OR and meets bitwise AND, giving zero failures on 475,800 pairs.

nodes.label: ℛ (the recovery operator)
nodes.rationale: A relaxation rather than a CSP closure: ℛ(X) is the smallest set cut out by pairwise monotone envelopes, so it adds cells the envelopes cannot distinguish rather than cells implied by the constraints.

nodes.label: E (the index defect measure)
nodes.rationale: E measures distance from Deville's staircase class and nothing else: E(ℛ) = 0 iff X is an intersection of staircases, and E = 0 owes its fibration — the same thirty-two elements give 4, 3, 2 or 0 depending on how they are fibred.

nodes.label: Deville's staircase class / connected row-convexity
nodes.rationale: (α,β)-monotone with α, β in {≤,≥} gives four corners; ℛ uses only (≤,≤), so E = 0 implies staircase but a staircase can have E = 750.

nodes.label: ℛ₄ (the four-orientation operator)
nodes.rationale: Adopted as a second operator so that E − E₄ reads as an orientation cost, separating 'not expressible' into outside-the-class and outside-ℛ's-corner.

nodes.label: Orientation cost (E − E₄)
nodes.rationale: Eight of ten indexed objects cost zero, so nothing the book concludes depends on the choice of corner; the parity rule costs 750, its whole defect, being the anti-diagonal.

nodes.label: The seed is a size, not a set
nodes.rationale: Six independent minimisations give six distinct seeds with zero cells in common, so anti-exchange fails: ℛ's closed sets are a Moore family and not a convex geometry, and 'the seed' names a cardinality.

nodes.label: The seed is constructible and need never be searched for
nodes.rationale: ℛ(X) is determined by φ̂ alone, so witnessing cells plus one per alphabet value share the envelopes and the closure; the seed is bounded by O(d² × cap depth), not by |Λ|.

nodes.label: A.cert (the certificate condition)
nodes.rationale: Proved, sourced to Tarski 1955: an open index does not close itself except where a certificate exhibits an operation on its coordinate system reaching a fixed point of ℛ. It admits RELABEL, RE-COORDINATISE, REFINE A FIBRATION and DROP A COORDINATE — and ADD A COORDINATE is not among them, which is the single cause of four closure failures.

nodes.label: A.staircls (held cells form a staircase)
nodes.rationale: A staircase of held cells is exactly the condition for E(ℛ) = 0, which is why the law index closes when ordered by locality of carrier.

nodes.label: A.19 (the seventeen generators)
nodes.rationale: Every generator is min{x ∈ Λ : x_c ≥ v} for one coordinate and one value, so the alphabet is defined rather than listed and has closed size Σ(|Aᵢ| − 1) = 17.

nodes.label: Binary, the seventh language admitted
nodes.rationale: Admitting {0,1}^17 as a language gives 7.07 bits of surplus per cell and zero failures on 475,800 pairs.

nodes.label: 2-decomposability (Q item U1 located)
nodes.rationale: E(X) = 0 is a named class in constraint satisfaction; the class was named in the literature and the graded count was not.

nodes.label: The tower (Λ₁ … Λ₁₃)
nodes.rationale: Closed exhaustively against every cell of its ambient box to 47,775,744 at Λ₁₃, replacing a form argument that had carried closure above Λ₁₀.

nodes.label: The method equation (F(1), F(−1))
nodes.rationale: Applied to a closed index it classifies cells as CONTAINS, MAY or CANNOT, because a monotone operator cannot bound a cell that exceeds every witnessed cell in rank.

nodes.label: RANK IS NOT REACH (the withdrawn six hundred)
nodes.rationale: Register 1610's 600 unreachable-but-unobstructed cells were withdrawn at 1611: all 600 carry 'derived by symmetry; no measurement required', and the true count of bound-open cells lacking an upper witness is zero.

nodes.label: Bergman's Double-projection Theorem
nodes.rationale: The book's central theorem A.2 — X closed ⟺ ℛ(X) = X — is this theorem specialised to products of chains: correct, and fifty years late.

nodes.label: Siggers / Larson on tight subdirect embeddings
nodes.rationale: Chain decompositions were applied to subdirect embeddings when Larson's correspondence is for tight ones; Siggers states the distinction and gives the Z₃ × Z₃ counterexample.

nodes.label: The Kreuzer–Skarke catalogue
nodes.rationale: Recorded as uncomputable because the whole file could not be read; a slice is specified exactly in print and ℛ applies to it — 208 cells, 540 predictions, none falsified. The obstacle was the catalogue, not the method.

nodes.label: The seven prime audits
nodes.rationale: The six existing audits were closed under self-reference — every one checked the book against the book — so none could see a citation pointing outside it; ATTRIBUTION was defined to break that closure.

nodes.label: The ARTEFACT audit
nodes.rationale: Exists because ℛ's U+1D4E1 and ⅅ's U+1D49F are carried by no DejaVu face: 107 blank boxes across 44 pages, and every audit then defined passed because every one read the source rather than the render.

nodes.label: The ATTRIBUTION audit
nodes.rationale: Found three attribution defects in three runs — Baker–Pixley, Bergman and Kimura et al.; then Racah 1942/1943; then Dunz 1911 — each cited in the text and absent from the References.

nodes.label: The COHERENCE audit
nodes.rationale: Passed all twenty-eight cross-references to §24.4 because every target existed, which is why a wildcard target is invisible to an existence check.

nodes.label: The figure audit
nodes.rationale: On its first run it found two figures numbered against the reading order and fifteen figures below print resolution at a median 164 dpi; the resolution defect was recorded in C.3 rather than repaired.

nodes.label: The whitespace audit
nodes.rationale: Its first measurement read the PDF text matrix as page geometry (median inked fraction 103%); its second counted characters and not images, flagging seven pages as empty at the head when all seven begin with a figure. The audit could not see the ink it was measuring.

nodes.label: The vacuous test (a check that compares a list to itself)
nodes.rationale: The magic-number check and the downset test both printed True having tested nothing; a test that would pass on anything establishes nothing.

nodes.label: The quantum-defect compendium
nodes.rationale: Defects are measured from series the source itself marks as unperturbed; bracketed Ritz and extrapolated levels are omitted because a defect computed from an extrapolated level is a defect computed from a defect.

nodes.label: P.lcollapse (the ℓ-ordering of defects)
nodes.rationale: The defect falls monotonically with ℓ even with a collapsing orbital mid-sequence, because collapse changes the SIZE of a defect and not its order.

nodes.label: P.coreblind (defects blind to the core's fine structure)
nodes.rationale: Confirmed where cores are 287 cm⁻¹ apart as well as 26,000 — four independent series on two limits all within 0.04.

nodes.label: P.selfsame (two disjoint n windows give the same defect)
nodes.rationale: The strongest internal check available: it compares one series to itself across a gap, where ℓ-ordering and J-consistency compare different series. Qualified rather than refuted by P.lens — valid only where the amplification is comparable across the windows.

nodes.label: P.lens (the defect is measured through a worsening lens near the limit)
nodes.rationale: δ depends on (limit − E), which shrinks as n² while the level's error does not, so fractional error grows as n³: a long series is precise at the bottom and blind at the top, and a six-member run at n = 8–13 beats a thirty-seven-member run at n = 20–56.

nodes.label: P.trunc (truncation widens a series)
nodes.rationale: Cutting a series at low n removes channels and widens what remains — right about truncation, and wrongly generalised to mean that longer is always better.

nodes.label: P.perturb (perturbed series widen and the source names the perturber)
nodes.rationale: Spreads of 0.15–0.21 in Si I nd coincide with the ASD leading-percentage column naming 3s.3p³ mixing fourteen per cent in; the gate is distinguishing unperturbed series from perturbed ones, not good data from bad.

nodes.label: P.jsplit / term-versus-J splitting
nodes.rationale: At ℓ = 3 f channels split by TERM and not by J — each J-pair agrees to 0.001 while terms separate by up to 0.048 — because the far electron feels the core's angular arrangement rather than its charge distribution.

nodes.label: The amplitude law and its ceiling M
nodes.rationale: Predicted the peak at u₀ = 3.894 and In I landed at 3.892 — the position right and the ceiling low by about a tenth, the excess being the p-channel running high rather than the amplitude being wrong.

nodes.label: u = ln(Nₑ/c^(2/3)) (the collapsing variable)
nodes.rationale: A collapse and not a better fit: species with wildly different (Nₑ, c) sharing Nₑ/c^(2/3) share a, collapsing 41 per-element constants onto one variable at r² 0.9920.

nodes.label: Thomas–Fermi scaling (the ⅔ exponent)
nodes.rationale: The ⅔ relating electron count to charge is attributed rather than claimed, and its authors' caveat is ours: the relation fails for neutral atoms and works in the cationic domain, exactly where our residuals bow.

nodes.label: The charge exponent is self-referential
nodes.rationale: Changing carrier from 1/√Nₑ to e^(−u/2) drove a fitted constant to unity (C′ = 1.0065), so the exponent of c contains c: the charge sets the rate at which its own influence decays.

nodes.label: The Pauli floor
nodes.rationale: Sound because it is an integer with no fitted number — and must be false as a function of u for the same reason.

nodes.label: Charge is the coordinate that absorbs
nodes.rationale: Every degeneracy found in the absorption audit was between a charge term and something else; c^(−C/√Nₑ) and c·lnNₑ are near-degenerate over the data's range, so a new cross term is absorbed rather than measured.

nodes.label: The penetration regime is an instrument, not an axis
nodes.rationale: It purifies every axis but is a FUNCTION of (Z, charge, ℓ), so adding it as a coordinate made every added cell a phantom (E = 56,168, exactly the cell count); partitioning on it destroyed the closure it was meant to improve, because cutting a staircase in two leaves neither piece one.

nodes.label: The law index closes when ordered by locality
nodes.rationale: Across all 120,960 orderings E runs 0 to 21 and 288 reach zero; the closing carrier order u < p < ℓ−ℓ_core < Z−T is monotone in how local the variable is.

nodes.label: The constant index (fourteen constants)
nodes.rationale: Every CENTRE is a small integer or half-integer and every SCALE is not; β = ⅔ is the only constant of arity three — the load-bearing constant, and the one that is attributed.

nodes.label: Six points chosen because they looked orderly
nodes.rationale: The ℓ-spread law fitted on six hand-picked species at r² 0.868 gave r² 0.044 on all nineteen — the same error as the four 'independent confirmations' of 1.23.

nodes.label: NIST ASD (and VALD, Kurucz, BRASS)
nodes.rationale: Re-graded referee flag 5 from 'no target' to 'targets identified, run not attempted': all four carry the designations the D1 tripwire needs.

nodes.label: The D1 tripwire
nodes.rationale: Specified in full at §16.3.1 and rejecting 150 of 216 offered assignments across s, p, d and f.

nodes.label: Λ_spectra (the spectra index on (Z, charge, ℓ))
nodes.rationale: Closes at E = 0 with Z = 119 and 120 present because c ≤ Z makes the whole set a staircase and mult is a fibration over N = Z − charge + 1; every T8 residue lives in the VALUE store, never in the coordinates.

nodes.label: store_gen.py
nodes.rationale: Carries the limit assignment and four statuses with no fifth — parent-matched, forced, positional, unwitnessed — and no fallback replaces the one R 1664 voided.

nodes.label: series_gen.py
nodes.rationale: Built because nothing on disk constructed (ℓ, term, parent) series from a raw table: the 554 stored series were staged by hand, so the store was never a census of its own species.

nodes.label: MEASUREMENTS-DERIVED.tsv
nodes.rationale: Generated beside the authored MEASUREMENTS.tsv rather than rewriting it, because §H.4 holds evidence instead of deleting it.

nodes.label: T8 — the limit assignment
nodes.rationale: Parent match is a string equality on the printed parent; where a parent's limit was never published the series CANNOT be defected, carried as a named bound — E measuring the world rather than the data.

nodes.label: T8-J (a J-resolved parent may borrow the parent ion's limit)
nodes.rationale: limit(J) = printed limit(J₀) + [E_ion(term,J) − E_ion(term,J₀)]. Applied NARROW — the term's limit must be printed — because the 145 old-void rows are the same operation one step wider, and widening is M's ruling, not a regex.

nodes.label: UNWITNESSED (a named bound, not a refusal)
nodes.rationale: The series is not undefected for want of trying: it requires a witnessed measurement science has yet to provide.

nodes.label: The positional reading of a limit
nodes.rationale: NIST's own table convention — series levels sit beneath the limit they converge to — adopted as a READING and named as one, guarded by the measured ladder_exceeds_limit column.

nodes.label: §H.4 — history stands and the bridge says so
nodes.rationale: Where a document states a figure true when written and now superseded, leave it and say so in the bridge; three occurrences were left standing at R 1656 for exactly this reason.

nodes.label: R 1685 — read the digest before stating work
nodes.rationale: Broken a third session running: the clause fails not for want of wording but because the first message of a session arrives before the bank does, so the opening turn should acknowledge the directives and state nothing else.

nodes.label: §2.9 — no silent default, and a relabel is not a rewrite
nodes.rationale: The 31 jj rows' mult = 0 is relabelled a null written in a language that has no S, which A.cert admits and which touches no coordinate of any index.

nodes.label: M.C2 (the modular-inclusion conjecture)
nodes.rationale: Regraded CONDITIONAL at source: what remains is not a parameter but a containment between two classes of spacetimes — whether the class admitting an ANE-vacuum with Reeh–Schlieder strictly contains the Killing horizons.

nodes.label: The Reeh–Schlieder property (condition four)
nodes.rationale: Cyclicity for the FULL algebra is automatic in a GNS representation; cyclicity for the EXTERIOR subalgebra is Reeh–Schlieder and does not follow from purity, which is why condition four is the remaining gap.

nodes.label: Half-sided modular inclusion ↔ chiral conformal net
nodes.rationale: Guido–Longo–Wiesbrock's bijection makes condition four a THEOREM rather than a hypothesis for a chiral net on the lightray, since the vacuum is cyclic and separating for each local algebra by locality.

nodes.label: The smeared ANE operators
nodes.rationale: Whether the distinguished boundary state is annihilated by them is a separate question from its Hadamard property, and the general smearing is a supertranslation rather than a translation.

nodes.label: Dappiaggi, Moretti and Pinamonti, 'Hadamard States from Light-like Hypersurfaces'
nodes.rationale: The register held this reference for four hundred entries filed as evidence of the difficulty, when the same programme is the construction of the witness — the reframing re-read a source already in hand.

nodes.label: Moretti, Commun. Math. Phys. 268 (2006) 727
nodes.rationale: Supplies positivity of the u-translation generator in every Bondi frame and a UNIQUENESS theorem for the invariant pure quasifree state, covering three of the four Borchers conditions.

nodes.label: The four Borchers conditions
nodes.rationale: Three are supplied from existing theorems — positivity, the causal inclusion, invariance with uniqueness — and standardness for the cut algebra is the one that is not.

nodes.label: The non-expanding horizon and its cuts
nodes.rationale: Ashtekar's conditions require H ≅ S × ℝ with generators along ℝ, so a cut is one cross-section — compact, two-dimensional, without boundary — and the product over it is indexed by a continuum.

nodes.label: Θ = 0 cannot define the relative boost
nodes.rationale: θ_ab = 0 is invariant under ℓ → a(y)ℓ, and a condition invariant under a group cannot fix that group's parameter; what it gives is a canonical map BETWEEN cuts, where a boost is a canonical scaling ALONG them.

nodes.label: Local Rindler frames (smoothness supplies the boost)
nodes.rationale: Smoothness plus the equivalence principle give a local boost Killing field to first order at any cut — which is the mechanism Θ = 0 was missing, and it is explicitly non-patchable to finite separation.

nodes.label: The continuous tensor product over the cut
nodes.rationale: Cyclicity of a product vector follows in a finite or countable tensor product, but horizon generators form a continuum and continuous products of type III factors are where such an argument needs care or fails. The object hands its remaining difficulty to operator algebras rather than gravity.

nodes.label: Hadamard is a microlocal (ultraviolet) condition
nodes.rationale: It is characterised by the wavefront set of the two-point distribution, where positivity of the translation generator is a condition on the entire spectrum — which is why the proposal conflating them is false before any computation.
